(ii) Adjoint of a diagonal matrix is also a diagonal matrix.

reasoning: The adjugate satisfies adj(A^T)=adj(A)^T for every square matrix.
Therefore adj(A)^T=adj(A^T)=adj(A), so adj(A) is symmetric.
For diagonal A, each off-diagonal cofactor is zero, because the corresponding minor has a zero row or column.
Thus the cofactor matrix and its transpose adj(A) are diagonal.
